KEY INSIGHTS


### The factors that drive AI decisions​


#### Review the economics, bottlenecks, and assumptions before your next AI deployment.​


Enterprise AI is not binary


The choices organizations face extend well beyond cloud versus on-premises and should be driven by scale and constraint intensity.


Portfolio approach prevents stranded capacity


A one-size-fits-all approach to AI infrastructure can produce stranded capacity or limit the performance and scalability of some workloads.


Economics flip at scale


When peak demand increasingly resembles steady demand, managing owned infrastructure often becomes more economical than consumption pricing.


Facility readiness is the bottleneck


Power availability, cooling capacity, and network fabric determine what can be deployed in an existing environment and on what timeline.


AI is becoming business-critical infrastructure


AI is rapidly becoming a load-bearing infrastructure for core business processes, changing the nature of infrastructure decisions.


Inference drives production demand


Production-scale generative inference can exceed the training demands of many traditional ML workloads because it becomes a continuous service on large models.
